title: Pulse-Level Compilation of Measurement-Free Recovery in Transmon Circuits
authors: Yi-Han Yu, Kai Xu, Heng Fan
abstract: Quantum error correction commonly relies on syndrome measurement, decoding, and conditional feedback. We numerically show that the conditional spectrum of an interacting transmon circuit can compile a local recovery rule into a fixed open-loop control cycle. In a four-bit repetition-code ring, the resulting input-independent control slows the decay of logical coherence under Pauli-\(X\) noise and stabilizes logical-one population under data relaxation relative to uncorrected references. Its local, bounded-degree architecture provides a hardware-native framework for extending compiled recovery control to larger quantum networks.
summary: This paper presents a method to implement Quantum Error Correction in superconducting transmon circuits using fixed, open-loop control pulses instead of traditional syndrome measurement and feedback. By compiling the recovery logic into a single waveform, the authors demonstrate protection against noise for a four-bit code ring, offering a scalable, hardware-efficient path toward fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the overhead associated with traditional Quantum Error Correction (QEC) by developing a method to compile syndrome measurement and recovery into a fixed, open-loop control waveform.
main_result: A local QEC rule can be compiled into a fixed, open-loop control cycle for transmon circuits, successfully slowing logical coherence decay and stabilizing logical populations for a four-bit repetition code ring.
method: The authors use spectral compilation, designing a composite waveform consisting of a swap operation and a conditional auxiliary transition to implement the recovery logic without real-time feedback.
model_or_system: The work is based on interacting transmon circuits, modeled as a four-site ring structure for a four-bit repetition code. The Hamiltonian and evolution are analyzed using time-dependent control pulses.
key_observables: Logical coherence ($C_Y$) and logical-one population ($P_{1L}$) decay rates, and the population transfer map for all 16 computational-basis inputs.
important_parameters: The system uses a fixed two-color scheduling for the ring update, and the cycle time is characterized by a $\mu$s scale.
main_assumptions: The residual error is assumed to be dominated by leakage due to spectral crowding, and the analysis focuses on the Z-basis rule, requiring further steps for phase-error correction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical process of fixed open-loop control transferring error records, detail the local compilation waveform, show the two-color pipelined schedule for the ring, and plot the decay of logical coherence and population under noise.
paper_structure: The paper develops models for local recovery subpulses, extends this to a full ring computation using a two-color schedule, and finally analyzes the performance of the resulting fixed waveform in a repeated-cycle error correction scheme.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, hardware-native blueprint for implementing fault-tolerant quantum computation by replacing complex, time-consuming feedback loops with fixed, engineered control pulses.
